lesson_scope: Two-body kinematics along the same vertical line under gravity; simultaneous and staggered launch conditions; algebraic collision heights and crossover times; relative speeds of approach and separation distance functions; intervals of co-directional vertical motion and apex configurations.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Time of collision for simultaneous upward throw and dropped particle

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Time of collision for simultaneous upward throw and dropped particle

hints: Write the height above ground for each particle at time $t$: $h_A = 20t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ and $h_B = 30 - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
At collision, $h_A = h_B$. Notice that the $-\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ terms cancel, leaving $20t = 30 \implies t = 1.5\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write expressions for the height above the ground of both particles at time $t$:
$$h_A = 20t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 20t - 5t^2$$
$$h_B = 30 - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 30 - 5t^2$$

Equate the two heights to find the time of collision:
$$20t - 5t^2 = 30 - 5t^2$$
$$20t = 30 \implies t = \frac{30}{20} = 1.5\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Express positions relative to ground level:
- Particle $A$ climbs while particle $B$ falls:
$$h_A = 20t - 5t^2$$
$$h_B = 30 - 5t^2$$

Solve for encounter time:
- Gravity affects both particles equally, so the quadratic terms cancel:
$$20t = 30 \implies t = 1.5\text{ s}$$
The particles collide after $1.5\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up height equations $h_A = 20t - 5t^2$ and $h_B = 30 - 5t^2$.
Equates $h_A = h_B$ to obtain $20t = 30 \implies t = 1.5\text{ s}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 2: Height of collision above the ground for simultaneous vertical encounter

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Height of collision above the ground for simultaneous vertical encounter

hints: The collision occurs at $t = 1.5\text{ s}$. Substitute $t = 1.5\text{ s}$ into either height expression.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the time of collision by equating positions:
$$20t = 30 \implies t = 1.5\text{ s}$$

Substitute $t = 1.5\text{ s}$ into the height equation for particle $B$ (or particle $A$):
$$h = 30 - 5(1.5^2) = 30 - 5(2.25) = 30 - 11.25 = 18.75\text{ m}$$
Check with particle $A$:
$$h = 20(1.5) - 5(1.5^2) = 30 - 11.25 = 18.75\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine time of meeting:
- Simultaneous closure at constant relative speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$t = \frac{30}{20} = 1.5\text{ s}$$

Compute elevation above ground:
- Evaluating position of either body at $t = 1.5\text{ s}$:
$$h = 30 - 5(2.25) = 18.75\text{ m}$$
The particles meet at an elevation of $18.75\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds collision time $t = 1.5\text{ s}$ and substitutes into $h_A$ or $h_B$.
Obtains collision height $h = 30 - 5(1.5^2) = 18.75\text{ m}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 3: Relative speed of approach between two vertically moving bodies

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Relative speed of approach between two vertically moving bodies

hints: Relative speed of approach between two bodies moving towards each other is the sum of their individual speeds.
Calculate $v_{\text{rel}} = 8 + 12 = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Choose vertically upwards as the positive direction:
$$v_A = +8\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad v_B = -12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the relative velocity of approach:
$$v_{\text{rel}} = v_A - v_B = 8 - (-12) = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{The relative speed of approach is } 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Assess direction of motion:
- The two bodies travel in opposite senses along the same line:
$$v_A = +8\text{ m s}^{-1}, \quad v_B = -12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Compute approach rate:
- Summing opposing speed components:
$$v_{\text{rel}} = 8 + 12 = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The distance between them decreases at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies that the bodies are moving towards each other and sums the speeds: $8 - (-12)$.
Obtains relative speed of approach $v_{\text{rel}} = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Vertical separation between two simultaneously projected particles

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Vertical separation between two simultaneously projected particles

hints: Because both particles experience the same gravitational acceleration, the $-\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ term cancels in the difference.
Distance between them is simply $(u_P - u_Q)t = (25 - 18)(2) = 7(2) = 14\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the height above the ground of each particle at $t = 2\text{ s}$:
$$h_P = 25(2) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(2^2) = 50 - 20 = 30\text{ m}$$
$$h_Q = 18(2) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(2^2) = 36 - 20 = 16\text{ m}$$

Subtract the heights to find the vertical separation distance:
$$d = h_P - h_Q = 30 - 16 = 14\text{ m}$$
Notice that this equals $(u_P - u_Q)t = (25 - 18)(2) = 14\text{ m}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Observe cancellation of gravity:
- Both bodies share identical acceleration $g$:
$$h_P - h_Q = (u_P - u_Q)t$$

Evaluate separation at $t = 2\text{ s}$:
- Speed difference times elapsed time:
$$d = (25 - 18) \times 2 = 7 \times 2 = 14\text{ m}$$
The particles are separated by $14\text{ m}$ after $2\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates positions $h_P = 25(2) - 5(4) = 30$ and $h_Q = 18(2) - 5(4) = 16$, or applies $\Delta h = (u_P - u_Q)t$.
Obtains separation distance $d = 30 - 16 = 14\text{ m}$.

- Particle $B$ begins moving upwards at $t = 1.0\text{ s}$
- Particle $A$ moves upwards for $0 < t < 2.4\text{ s}$
- Particle $B$ moves upwards for $1.0 < t < 3.0\text{ s}$
$$\text{Both move upwards for } 1.0\text{ s} < t < 2.4\text{ s} \quad (\text{duration } 1.4\text{ s})$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 6: Time elapsed when separation between sequentially dropped particles reaches a target distance

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Time elapsed when separation between sequentially dropped particles reaches a target distance

hints: At time $t$ ($t \ge 1$), distance fallen by $A$ is $s_A = 5t^2$, and distance fallen by $B$ is $s_B = 5(t - 1)^2$.
Set $s_A - s_B = 25$: $5t^2 - 5(t^2 - 2t + 1) = 10t - 5 = 25 \implies 10t = 30 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the distances fallen downwards by both particles at time $t$ ($t \ge 1$):
$$s_A = \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 5t^2$$
$$s_B = \frac{1}{2}(10)(t - 1)^2 = 5(t^2 - 2t + 1) = 5t^2 - 10t + 5$$

Set the vertical separation to $25\text{ m}$ and solve for $t$:
$$s_A - s_B = 5t^2 - (5t^2 - 10t + 5) = 10t - 5$$
$$10t - 5 = 25 \implies 10t = 30 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate separation equation:
- The distance gap between the dropped masses:
$$s_A - s_B = 5t^2 - 5(t - 1)^2 = 10t - 5$$

Solve for target separation:
- Setting the gap to $25\text{ m}$:
$$10t - 5 = 25 \implies 10t = 30 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$
The separation reaches $25\text{ m}$ after $3\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses vertical separation as $5t^2 - 5(t - 1)^2 = 10t - 5$.
Solves $10t - 5 = 25$ to obtain $t = 3\text{ s}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 1: Upward projection and delayed vertical drop along the same line

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Upward projection and delayed vertical drop along the same line

hints: Form equations of motion: $h_A = 20t - 5t^2$ and $h_B = 35 - 5(t - 1)^2$.
Equate $h_A = h_B$ to find $t = 3\text{ s}$, then evaluate height: $h = 20(3) - 5(3^2) = 15\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the height equations for both particles in terms of time $t$ from the launch of $A$ ($t \ge 1$):
$$h_A = 20t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 20t - 5t^2$$
$$h_B = 35 - \frac{1}{2}(10)(t - 1)^2 = 35 - 5(t^2 - 2t + 1) = 30 + 10t - 5t^2$$

Equate the two heights to find the time of collision:
$$20t - 5t^2 = 30 + 10t - 5t^2$$
$$10t = 30 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

Calculate the height above the ground at collision:
$$h = 20(3) - 5(3^2) = 60 - 45 = 15\text{ m}$$
Check with particle $B$:
$$h = 35 - 5(2^2) = 35 - 20 = 15\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate altitude equations:
- Particle $A$ climbs from the ground:
$$h_A = 20t - 5t^2$$
- Particle $B$ is dropped from $35\text{ m}$ after a $1\text{ s}$ delay:
$$h_B = 35 - 5(t - 1)^2 = 30 + 10t - 5t^2$$

Solve for encounter:
- Equating positions cancels the gravity terms:
$$20t = 30 + 10t \implies 10t = 30 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$
- Evaluating altitude:
$$h = 20(3) - 45 = 15\text{ m}$$
The collision occurs at an elevation of $15\text{ m}$ after $3\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses height of $A$ as $h_A = 20t - 5t^2$ and height of $B$ as $h_B = 35 - 5(t - 1)^2$.
Equates $h_A = h_B$ to form $20t - 5t^2 = 30 + 10t - 5t^2$ and solves for $t$.
Obtains collision time $t = 3\text{ s}$ and collision height $h = 15\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Upward projection and delayed vertical drop along the same line

hints: For particle $A$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$: $v_A = u - gt = 20 - 10(3) = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The negative sign indicates it is moving downwards.
For particle $B$ after falling for $2\text{ s}$: $v_B = -gt = -10(2) = -20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Both particles are descending at impact.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the velocity of particle $A$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$v_A = u - gt = 20 - 10(3) = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{Particle } A \text{ has speed } 10\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ directed vertically downwards}$$

Calculate the velocity of particle $B$ at $t = 3\text{ s}$ (having fallen for $t - 1 = 2\text{ s}$):
$$v_B = 0 - 10(2) = -20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{Particle } B \text{ has speed } 20\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ directed vertically downwards}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compute velocity of particle $A$:
- Particle $A$ passed its apex at $t = 2\text{ s}$ and is descending:
$$v_A = 20 - 10(3) = -10\text{ m s}^{-1} \implies 10\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ downwards}$$

Compute velocity of particle $B$:
- Particle $B$ has accelerated downwards for $2\text{ s}$:
$$v_B = 0 - 10(2) = -20\text{ m s}^{-1} \implies 20\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ downwards}$$
Both particles are falling at collision, with speeds of $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $v = u - gt$ to evaluate velocity of $A$ at $t = 3$ and velocity of $B$ at $t - 1 = 2$.
Obtains speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ directed downwards for $A$ and speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ directed downwards for $B$.

walkthrough.text:

$$0 = 20 - 10t \implies 10t = 20 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$$

Calculate the height of both particles at $t = 2\text{ s}$ and find their separation:
$$h_P = 30(2) - 5(2^2) = 60 - 20 = 40\text{ m}$$
$$h_Q = 20(2) - 5(2^2) = 40 - 20 = 20\text{ m}$$
$$d = h_P - h_Q = 40 - 20 = 20\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find apex time for particle $Q$:
- Velocity vanishes at:
$$t = \frac{20}{10} = 2\text{ s}$$

Compute particle separation:

$$d = 10 \times 2 = 20\text{ m}$$
The particles are separated by $20\text{ m}$ at the instant $Q$ reaches its peak.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 2: Simultaneous vertical projection with differing initial velocities

hints: Particle $Q$ returns to the ground when $h_Q = 0 \implies 20t - 5t^2 = 0 \implies t_1 = 4\text{ s}$.
Evaluate position and velocity of $P$ at $t = 4\text{ s}$: $h_P = 30(4) - 5(16) = 40\text{ m}$ and $v_P = 30 - 10(4) = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (downwards).

walkthrough.text:
Find the time $t_1$ when particle $Q$ lands on the ground:
$$h_Q = 20t - 5t^2 = 0 \implies 5t(4 - t) = 0$$
$$t_1 = 4\text{ s}$$

Calculate the height of particle $P$ at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$h_P = 30(4) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(4^2) = 120 - 80 = 40\text{ m}$$

Calculate the velocity of particle $P$ at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$v_P = 30 - 10(4) = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{Particle } P \text{ has speed } 10\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ directed vertically downwards}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find flight duration of $Q$:
- Symmetrical flight gives twice the apex time:
$$t_1 = 2 \times 2 = 4\text{ s}$$

Determine position and velocity of $P$:
- Altitude at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$h_P = 30(4) - 5(16) = 40\text{ m}$$
- Velocity at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$v_P = 30 - 40 = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
When $Q$ lands, particle $P$ is $40\text{ m}$ above the ground, descending at $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Solves $20t - 5t^2 = 0$ for non-zero root to obtain return time $t_1 = 4\text{ s}$.
Calculates height of $P$: $h_P = 30(4) - 5(16) = 40\text{ m}$.
Applies $v = u - gt$ to find $v_P = 30 - 10(4) = -10\text{ m s}^{-1}$, stating speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ directed downwards.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the height of particle $A$ at time $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$h_A = 25(3) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(3^2) = 75 - 45 = 30\text{ m}$$
$$\text{The common height is } 30\text{ m}$$

Determine the flight time of particle $B$ at this instant:
$$t_B = 3 - 2 = 1\text{ s}$$
Set $h_B(1) = 30\text{ m}$:
$$u(1) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(1^2) = 30$$
$$u - 5 = 30 \implies u = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find meeting elevation:
- Evaluating position of particle $A$ after $3\text{ s}$:
$$h = 25(3) - 5(9) = 75 - 45 = 30\text{ m}$$

Determine launch velocity of $B$:
- Particle $B$ has travelled for only $1\text{ s}$ to reach $30\text{ m}$:
$$u(1) - 5(1) = 30 \implies u = 35\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Particle $B$ is projected at $35\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ downwards with $u = 0$, $a = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $s = 45\text{ m}$:
$$45 = \frac{1}{2}(10)t_P^2 = 5t_P^2$$
$$t_P^2 = 9 \implies t_P = 3\text{ s}$$

Calculate the impact speed of $P$ using $v = u + at$:
$$v_P = 0 + 10(3) = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find flight duration for $P$:
- Dropped from $45\text{ m}$ under gravity:
$$45 = 5t_P^2 \implies t_P = 3\text{ s}$$

Find impact speed:
- Accelerating from rest:
$$v_P = 10 \times 3 = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Particle $P$ hits the ground after $3\text{ s}$ at $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 4: Simultaneous ground arrival for dropped and projected particles

hints: Downwards motion of $Q$: displacement is $s = 30\text{ m}$, initial speed is $u = 5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and acceleration is $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Apply $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$: $30 = 5t_Q + 5t_Q^2 \implies t_Q^2 + t_Q - 6 = 0 \implies (t_Q - 2)(t_Q + 3) = 0 \implies t_Q = 2\text{ s}$.
Since both hit at the same time: $T + t_Q = t_P \implies T + 2 = 3 \implies T = 1\text{ s}$.
Calculate impact speed: $v_Q = 5 + 10(2) = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the displacement equation for particle $Q$ falling through $30\text{ m}$:
$$s = ut_Q + \frac{1}{2}gt_Q^2 \implies 30 = 5t_Q + 5t_Q^2$$
$$5t_Q^2 + 5t_Q - 30 = 0 \implies t_Q^2 + t_Q - 6 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation for the duration of $Q$'s flight:
$$(t_Q - 2)(t_Q + 3) = 0 \implies t_Q = 2\text{ s}$$
Since both particles hit the ground at the same instant:
$$T + t_Q = t_P \implies T + 2 = 3 \implies T = 1\text{ s}$$

Calculate the impact speed of particle $Q$ using $v = u + at$:
$$v_Q = 5 + 10(2) = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Alternatively:
$$v_Q^2 = 5^2 + 2(10)(30) = 25 + 600 = 625 \implies v_Q = \sqrt{625} = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find flight duration of $Q$:
- Setting position quadratic:
$$5t_Q^2 + 5t_Q - 30 = 0 \implies t_Q^2 + t_Q - 6 = 0$$
$$(t_Q - 2)(t_Q + 3) = 0 \implies t_Q = 2\text{ s}$$

Compute time delay $T$:
- Synchronizing landing times:
$$T = t_P - t_Q = 3 - 2 = 1\text{ s}$$

Determine collision speed:
- Final velocity of $Q$:
$$v_Q = 5 + 10(2) = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Particle $Q$ is thrown $1\text{ s}$ after $P$ and strikes the ground at $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up quadratic for flight time of $Q$: $30 = 5t_Q + 5t_Q^2$.
Solves quadratic to obtain $t_Q = 2\text{ s}$ and finds delay $T = 3 - 2 = 1\text{ s}$.
Calculates impact speed $v_Q = 5 + 10(2) = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:

  $$\text{Moving upwards for } 0 < t < 1.6\text{ s}$$
  $$\text{Moving downwards for } 1.6 < t < 3.2\text{ s}$$
- For $Q$ (launched at $t = 0.8\text{ s}$, flight duration $4.0\text{ s}$):
  $$\text{Moving upwards for } 0.8 < t < 2.8\text{ s}$$
  $$\text{Moving downwards for } 2.8 < t < 4.8\text{ s}$$

Find the intersection where both move upwards:
$$\text{Upward interval: } (0, 1.6) \cap (0.8, 2.8) = (0.8, 1.6)$$
$$0.8\text{ s} < t < 1.6\text{ s}$$

Find the intersection where both move downwards:
$$\text{Downward interval: } (1.6, 3.2) \cap (2.8, 4.8) = (2.8, 3.2)$$
$$2.8\text{ s} < t < 3.2\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:

$$\text{Ascent: } 0 < t < 1.6\text{ s}, \quad \text{Descent: } 1.6 < t < 3.2\text{ s}$$

$$\text{Ascent: } 0.8 < t < 2.8\text{ s}, \quad \text{Descent: } 2.8 < t < 4.8\text{ s}$$

- Both climb simultaneously during:
$$0.8\text{ s} < t < 1.6\text{ s}$$

Identify simultaneous downward motion:

$$2.8\text{ s} < t < 3.2\text{ s}$$
The particles share the same direction for $0.8 < t < 1.6\text{ s}$ (up) and $2.8 < t < 3.2\text{ s}$ (down).

hints: Express the height of particle $A$ at time $t$: $h_A = Ut - 5t^2$.
For particle $B$, time elapsed is $(t - 1)$: $h_B = 28(t - 1) - 5(t - 1)^2$.
Equate $h_A = h_B$: $Ut - 5t^2 = 38t - 5t^2 - 33 \implies (38 - U)t = 33 \implies t = \frac{33}{38 - U}$.
Set $t = 3\text{ s}$: $3(38 - U) = 33 \implies 38 - U = 11 \implies U = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the vertical position equations for both particles:
$$h_A = Ut - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = Ut - 5t^2$$
$$h_B = 28(t - 1) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(t - 1)^2 = 28(t - 1) - 5(t^2 - 2t + 1)$$
$$h_B = 28t - 28 - 5t^2 + 10t - 5 = 38t - 5t^2 - 33$$

Equate the heights to find the meeting time $t$:
$$Ut - 5t^2 = 38t - 5t^2 - 33$$
$$Ut = 38t - 33 \implies (38 - U)t = 33$$
$$t = \frac{33}{38 - U}$$

Substitute the given meeting time $t = 3\text{ s}$ to find $U$:
$$3 = \frac{33}{38 - U} \implies 3(38 - U) = 33$$
$$38 - U = 11 \implies U = 38 - 11 = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate altitude equations:
- Particle $A$:
$$h_A = Ut - 5t^2$$
- Particle $B$ delayed by $1\text{ s}$:
$$h_B = 28(t - 1) - 5(t - 1)^2 = 38t - 5t^2 - 33$$

Derive meeting relation:
- Cancelling gravity:
$$(38 - U)t = 33 \implies t = \frac{33}{38 - U}$$

Solve for launch speed $U$:
- Setting $t = 3\text{ s}$:
$$3(38 - U) = 33 \implies U = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Particle $A$ must be projected at $27\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Simplifies to $(38 - U)t = 33$ to show $t = \frac{33}{38 - U}$.
Substitutes $t = 3$ into $3(38 - U) = 33$ to obtain $U = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

- Difference in landing times:

hints: Write positions relative to ground: $h_P = 25t - 5t^2$ and $h_Q = H - 5t^2$.
Distance between them is $h_Q - h_P = (H - 5t^2) - (25t - 5t^2) = H - 25t$.
Passing occurs when distance is zero, so $H = 25t$.
Set height of $P$ to $20\text{ m}$: $25t - 5t^2 = 20 \implies t^2 - 5t + 4 = 0 \implies (t - 1)(t - 4) = 0$.
Since $P$ is moving upwards ($v_P > 0$), select $t = 1\text{ s}$. Then $H = 25(1) = 25\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the positions of both particles above the ground at time $t$:
$$h_P = 25t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 25t - 5t^2$$
$$h_Q = H - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = H - 5t^2$$
Find the vertical separation distance:
$$s(t) = h_Q - h_P = (H - 5t^2) - (25t - 5t^2) = H - 25t$$

Find the time $t$ when particle $P$ is at height $20\text{ m}$ moving upwards:
$$25t - 5t^2 = 20 \implies 5t^2 - 25t + 20 = 0$$
$$t^2 - 5t + 4 = 0 \implies (t - 1)(t - 4) = 0$$
$$\text{For upward motion } (v_P > 0): \quad t = 1\text{ s}$$

At passing, the separation is zero:
$$s(1) = H - 25(1) = 0 \implies H = 25\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate linear separation equation:
- Relative velocity is constant at $-25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s(t) = H - 25t$$

Find time of crossing:
- Reaching $20\text{ m}$ on upward climb:
$$25t - 5t^2 = 20 \implies t = 1\text{ s}, \; 4\text{ s}$$
- Upward motion corresponds to $t = 1\text{ s}$.

Solve for tower height:
- Zero separation at $t = 1\text{ s}$:
$$H = 25(1) = 25\text{ m}$$
The tower has a height of $25\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses separation as $(H - 5t^2) - (25t - 5t^2) = H - 25t$.
Sets $25t - 5t^2 = 20$ and solves for upward crossing time $t = 1\text{ s}$.
Substitutes $t = 1$ into $H - 25t = 0$ to obtain $H = 25\text{ m}$.
